THE SPACE BETWEEN LOOKING & KNOWING

Similar is a starting point.
The details tell the story.

Two garments can look alike and require different work. Crumble connects visual discovery to construction details, reviewable evidence and your operation time library.

01 / COLLECT

A collection
with context.

Bring in your product records and multiple image views. Keep source details, image rights and immutable evidence snapshots together.

02 / COMPARE

Find the likeness.
Locate the difference.

Search by photo or description with the fashion encoder. Compare parts side by side and distinguish verified details from uncertain proposals.

03 / REVIEW

with evidence.

SNAPSHOTS + LIBRARY VERSION

A SMALL CHANGE. A DIFFERENT PROCESS.

From a changed part
to a time question.

Standard Minute Value (SMV) describes the standard time for an operation under defined conditions. Crumble suggests how mapped operation time changes when the design changes.

Factory methods, fabrics, machinery and unseen construction matter. Your time studies supply the standards.

Change the design yourself →
OPERATION CHANGE / EXAMPLEMINUTES
Remove short-sleeve hems−2 × 0.25–0.35 min
−0.70 to −0.50
Add long-sleeve cuffs+2 × 0.80–1.10 min
+1.60 to +2.20
Add two patch pockets+2 × 0.60–0.90 min
+1.20 to +1.80
Mapped time change+2.10–3.50 min

Invented demo times. An illustrative mapped delta, not a total garment SMV or factory estimate.

CONFIDENCE STARTS WITH CLARITY

Evidence over
assumptions.

A match is a lead.
Visual similarity needs review. It does not establish copying, ownership or which design came first.
Unknown stays unknown.
A hidden pocket or an unseen lining is not a confirmed absence. Evidence states are explicit.
Useful before perfect.
This is a working alpha for local use and pilots. Broad retrieval accuracy and factory SMV accuracy remain to be validated.
